column3: RE-PINNED 2026-08-02 (audit): the previous pin named an INVALID reading and is replaced by the SATURATED relational one, which is currently a MISS. WHY THE OLD PIN WAS INVALID: its `And(§(kind_of(§)), prep_with(...))` was derived only through the `fin_any` VP-adjunct ERASURE. Witnessed in the chart: `associated` seeds a 1-place `S[dcl,pss]\NP` (past participle, ACTIVE/perfect) at sense-rank 1; no `is` entry selects a SATURATED `S[pss]\NP` (is_copula takes `adj`, is_prog `ger`, is_passive_by `pass`, is_passive the UNSATURATED `(S[pss]\NP)/NP`) — deliberately, so `*X is affected Y` stays out (lexicon-ontology.esl Fin/pss vs pass). The `with`-adjunct applied to that `pss` clause returned `S[dcl,fin_any]\NP`, erasing the feature, and the erased clause then satisfied ALL FOUR of the copula's saturated slots at once (adj/ger/pass/bse), witnessed in cell[1..9]. So the reading was licensed by a voice-feature violation. Removing the erasure (the VP-adjunct enumeration, this baseline) correctly removes it. WHY THE NEW PIN: every reading of this unit strands `with responses ...` as a free ADJUNCT conjunct, leaving `associated` under-saturated — `associated with` is a two-place relation and the relatum must BIND. The pinned skeleton is that reading, one predication with no top-level `And` and no separate `prep_with`. It was MEASURED, not invented: experiments/parsing/probes/assoc-stative-with.esl produces it (gloss `Microsatellite Instability associate a notable response to Immune Checkpoint Blockade`), gap 0, skeletons 160 -> 154, and collapses this unit 8 skeletons -> 2. KNOWN MISS until the governed frame ships: `associated` is NOT a WordNet adjective lemma (index.adj 0, unlike dependent/essential/concordant), so the `associated<TAB>with` row in adjective-frames.tsv NEVER FIRES — `governed_preposition` is reached only from `push_adj` over ADJECTIVE synset words. The verb `associate` (00713167) does carry frames 17/31, both naming `with`, but `classify` collapses 14|15|16|17|18|19|31 into a preposition-less Ditransitive and discards it. Do NOT re-pin to a currently-produced sibling: `gt(deg_assoc(MSI), std)` asserts MSI is associated to a degree above standard with NO relatum, which the sentence does not claim.
